_comment: DRAFT, NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED. A starting point for abdominal ultrasound. Have a sonographer or radiologist review and adapt every list to your exam types and house style before use. See README.md in this folder.

us: The lesion is T2 hyperintense with low T1 signal.
There is restricted diffusion on DWI sequences.
The mass demonstrates avid enhancement after gadolinium administration.
Bone window images demonstrate no cortical erosion.
Coronal reformats confirm the extent of the abnormality.

abdomen_us: The cerebral hemispheres show no acute infarct.
The thyroid gland is normal in size and echotexture.
The aortic valve leaflets are thin and mobile.
The visualized cervical spinal cord is normal in calibre.
Compared to the prior examination, the hepatic lesion has enlarged from 12 mm to 21 mm.
The previously described gallbladder sludge has resolved in the interval.
New ascites has developed since the prior study.
Interval increase in the size of the renal cyst is noted.
The previously noted hydronephrosis has improved since the earlier examination.
The spleen is normal in size.
The abdominal aorta is of normal calibre where visualised.

morphology_swap._comment: Echogenicity is ultrasound's density/signal; the built-in list covers CT and MR terms only.
